title: DeepONet: Learning nonlinear operators for identifying differential equations based on the universal approximation theorem of operators
layout_note: A 2 x 2 grid of lettered panels: A (inputs & output: u sampled at sensors plus y into one 'Network' box giving G(u)(y)), B (training data: dashed input curves with sensor dots mapped by an arrow G to dashed output curves), C (stacked DeepONet: p branch nets plus one trunk net) and D (unstacked DeepONet: one branch net plus one trunk net). C and D share one skeleton and differ only in the branch side, so the bottom row is a side-by-side comparison.
grouping: No frames around panels: each is set off by whitespace and a bold letter with a plain title (A Inputs & Output, B Training data, C Stacked DeepONet, D Unstacked DeepONet). Inside C and D, the branch outputs b1..bp and the trunk outputs t1..tp each sit in a tall thin rectangle, one above the other, both converging on a circled multiply.
shapes_depth: Flat square-cornered boxes: networks filled light lavender-blue with thin black outlines and sans-serif labels; the sensor-value vector u(x1)...u(xm) is a white box listing math entries; scalar outputs b_i and t_i are small grey-filled circles in a column box; the merge is a grey circle with a multiplication sign. Data in B are dashed curves with black dots marking sampling points.
proposed_highlight: Every network box (Network, Branch net, Trunk net) is the one lavender fill in the figure; the DeepONet itself is named in the titles of C and D, and the generic black-box 'Network' of panel A is redrawn in C and D as the branch/trunk pair meeting at a product node.
lesson: State the problem as a single black-box panel first, then redraw that box as the proposed two-network decomposition in the panels below, using the same fill for every learned network so the reader maps the black box onto its parts.

arrangement.units: Four unframed panels in a 2 x 2 grid, each headed by a bold letter and a plain title; the bottom two (stacked vs unstacked DeepONet) share an identical skeleton.
arrangement.inputs_as: math symbols u and y with arrows; u expands into a white box listing its sensor values u(x1) ... u(xm); panel B draws input functions as dashed curves with sensor dots
arrangement.shared: the trunk net and the product node are drawn identically in C and D; only the branch side changes (p branch nets vs one)

taxonomy.task: learning nonlinear operators between function spaces
taxonomy.note: modality: the inputs are functions sampled at fixed sensor points (1-D curves) plus query coordinates y; time-series is the closest list item, there is no 'function' modality.

core.what: panels C and D draw the stacked and unstacked DeepONet as the same branch/trunk skeleton side by side, differing only in p stacked branch nets vs one branch net fanning out to p outputs

relations.form: C and D side by side with identical trunk halves and identical product node, the left showing Branch net_1 ... Branch net_p stacked and the right one Branch net with arrows fanning to b_1 ... b_p
a framed column of branch outputs b_1..b_p and a framed column of trunk outputs t_1..t_p converge on one circled-x node producing G(u)(y)
branch path (u sampled at sensors) in the upper half and trunk path (y) in the lower half of each panel, both running left to right
panel B draws the training data as dashed function curves with sensor dots x_1..x_m on the left and output curves with random locations y on the right, joined by an arrow G

channels.colour: lavender = a learned network (Network, Branch net, Trunk net) in every panel; grey circles = network outputs b_k, t_k
channels.shape: rectangle = network or a column of sampled values u(x_i); grey circle = scalar output; circled x = inner product
channels.line: solid arrows = data flow; dashed curves in B = functions, not flow
channels.frame: a tall rectangle groups each output column (b's, t's) and the sensor-value list; panels A-D have letters but no frames

quality.strengths: The two architectures are drawn as matched panels with the same glyphs, so the single difference (branch stacking) is the visible difference; the branch and trunk outputs are drawn as named representations b_k and t_k between their networks and the product that combines them; lavender means 'learned network' everywhere.
quality.weaknesses: Panel B's curves and vertical ellipses are loosely placed and read as a sketch next to the tidy block diagrams; panel A repeats the problem statement with an opaque 'Network' box; the outputs from the b and t columns leave from the column edge as long diagonals to the product node.

insights.structure: A 2 x 2 grid where the top row states the problem (black-box Network; training curves) and the bottom row draws two variants of the same branch/trunk skeleton side by side.
insights.data: The input function is a white box listing its sampled values u(x1)...u(xm), branch and trunk outputs are columns of small grey circles b1..bp and t1..tp in tall thin boxes, and training data in panel B are dashed curves with dots at the sensor locations.
insights.emphasis: All learned networks share one lavender fill, and the bottom panels differ only in the branch side (p stacked branch nets vs one branch net fanning out to p outputs), so the stacked/unstacked distinction is the visible difference.
insights.flow: Each panel reads left to right: the branch path runs along the top and the trunk path along the bottom, and both columns' outputs slant down/up into a circled multiply that emits G(u)(y) on the right.
insights.avoid: Panels have no frames and the panel B curves are loosely placed with ellipses (vertical dots) for 'more samples', so B reads as a sketch next to the tidy block diagrams.

notes: Venue written as arXiv: no venue printed on the first page; Nature Machine Intelligence (2021) is remembered. year = arXiv preprint year (1910.03193). The automatic crop (fig1.png) also included the Theorem 1 statement and equation above the figure; the card describes and measures a trimmed copy holding only panels A-D (crops/1910.03193/fig1-panels.png, rows 520-1350 of fig1.png). Elements 'other': sensor-dot curve sketches in panel B.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
